topic: Shared file tail behavior with emulated 16 KiB pages
status: unresolved compatibility; shared-tail extension blocked by native MM invariants; candidate remains provisional
evidence: Pinned Goldfish x86_64_16k_cmdline.txt positively enables page_shift=14. ACK b3c77090341c extends file/shmem EOF to an emulated-page boundary and permits shared file VMAs in do_anonymous_page. Source review of do_anonymous_page, do_wp_page, wp_pfn_shared, wp_page_reuse and vm_normal_page shows the read-zero-page/shared-write route can make the global zero page writable; shared page_mkwrite and anonymous reverse mapping also need a coherent design. Restore the LTS VM_SHARED guard in c75a4c447656 while preserving private file-tail emulation and native 4 KiB behavior. This is a documented security-driven compatibility limit, not an absence-of-consumer finding. Determine whether to implement shared cache-backed tail pages or otherwise preserve Android shared mapping expectations safely; full runtime validation is out of current scope.

topic: Pagemap aggregate metadata under page-size emulation
status: resolved source-selection decision with known lossy metadata limits; runtime not verified
evidence: Full local 1b1a4ce9cfb1 explicitly suppresses PFN and swap identities because independent base-page identities cannot be encoded in one entry. Preserve this ACK representation instead of inventing a shared offset: local procmeminfo ReadVmaStats stores each reported swap offset, and libsmapinfo treats equal offsets as genuinely shared swap slots. Fabricating offset zero would falsely merge unrelated slots. Therefore pagemap-derived swap identity/accounting is intentionally unavailable under emulation, an existing ACK limitation, not proof of absent consumers; native 4 KiB reporting and separate native smaps byte accounting remain. pageacct.cpp explicitly has an x86 non-4096 PFN fallback. The historical claim that UFFD-WP is unavailable is not valid as a kernel assumption: actual config enables USERFAULTFD/HAVE_ARCH_USERFAULTFD_WP, native fs/userfaultfd.c is retained, and local Linux selftests inspect PM_UFFD_WP. 110e353eded3 preserves UFFD-WP and guard status with the existing ACK any-subpage OR convention. This reports presence somewhere in the group, not exact per-subpage metadata or wholly exclusive ownership. Native authorization and page-table operation paths remain. d65b1b963b41 fixes offset/count/lseek/pread consistently in the file reader. Extracted reader/aggregation tests cover 64 flag combinations, original failure controls and native-mode identity; no runtime userfaultfd or Android tools executed. Local commit-message link r.android.com/3424862 was not accessed.

topic: Large-folio fault-around and ELF padding boundaries
status: resolved source-selection decision; preserve existing ACK and LTS granularity, runtime not verified
evidence: Exact full-function comparison establishes that filemap_map_folio_range, filemap_map_pmd, finish_fault, do_set_pmd and thp_vma_suitable_order are identical in pinned ACK, LTS, normalized ACK and port. Thus the large-folio expansion is existing behavior on both inputs, not a regression introduced by the port. Keep native reference/accounting/PMD behavior and the ACK do_fault_around padding-fault skip plus requested-range clamp. The hint limits requested fault-around; it is not a strict prohibition on every larger-folio mapping or access to the real VMA. Local bionic linker_phdr.cpp DropPaddingPages treats this as MADV_DONTNEED memory/reclaim optimization, not a permission change. A new global THP constraint would add behavior absent from both inputs and is unnecessary to preserve their current compatibility. Smaps partial-range double counting is independently corrected in 20730118bf05. Evidence: evidence/large-folio-padding-comparison.json and complete local cd8dfe2cb388 patch. No runtime fault/THP test or remote access.

topic: DMA-buf accounting after nonfatal record allocation failure
status: cross-file failure behavior under review; VMA lifecycle candidates remain provisional
evidence: Full local __dma_buf_account_task, preload, unaccount, fd_install, do_dup2, dma_buf_mmap/internal, __split_vma and copy_vma were examined. Preload may fail before finding an already existing record. fd_install/mmap/split/copy deliberately log and continue without a count; later close/unmap decrements any existing record, so failure can undercount other still-live references. These counters are statistics, separate from the native file/buffer lifetime references, but local lmkd uses them in victim sizing. Need decide whether to retain/document ACK best-effort OOM accounting or adapt failure tracking without changing successful mmap/fd-install contracts. No actual allocation fault, mmap or LMK test has run. Prior path review explicitly described nonfatal errors but did not establish balanced counts after such a failure. No source change for this question yet; no remote access.
